chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ ابْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ، عَنْ حَمَّادِ بْنِ عُثْمَانَ، عَنِ الْحَلَبِيِّ وَزُرَارَةَ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الصَّبِيِّ مَتَى يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ؟

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi and Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the prayer over the child, when is it prayed over him?

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ: إِذَا عَقَلَ الصَّلَاةَ. قُلْتُ: مَتَى تَجِبُ الصَّلَاةُ عَلَيْهِ؟ فَقَالَ: إِذَا كَانَ ابْنَ سِتِّ سِنِينَ، وَالصِّيَامُ إِذَا أَطَاقَهُ.

translations.en: He said: When he understands the prayer. I said: When is prayer obligatory on him? He said: When he is a child of six years, and fasting is when he has the strength for it.

en.summary: This hadith delineates the stages of legal responsibility (taklif) by distinguishing between the age of understanding (aql) for ritual acts like funeral prayer and the specific age of six for the obligation of fasting and personal prayer. In Shia jurisprudence, this reflects the principle that while full maturity (bulugh) is marked by puberty, preparatory obligations begin earlier to train the child, with the age of six serving as a key benchmark for the onset of these duties.
en.seo_question: At what age does prayer and fasting become obligatory for children in Shia jurisprudence?

key_terms.يُطِيقُهُ: He has the strength/capacity for it
